utterances.text: It was around the 20th, not later than the 20th. I'm not sure really. Perhaps give or take two or three days, because it last -- because he stayed in the hospital for some five or six days. I visited him once. So it must have been until the 25th of July, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, in the light of your previous answer, not to repeat it again, I will ask you once again: When were you and Zoran Zigic sent away from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: We were sent away from -- I was fired between the 13th and the 14th.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know when was Zigic fired?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, if I quit on the 14th and he was -- it was the 13th. It was -- he left one day before me because that last day I did not see him in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you know in which department, in which ward of the Prijedor hospital was Zoran Zigic treated?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: In the surgical department where all the wounded were.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know who treated him?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Dr. Barudzija, a well-known doctor in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when Zigic was discharged from the hospital, did you continue to see him around?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: When he was discharged from the hospital, I heard that he went to the Gradac front line.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I know it very well, because in Prijedor, there was a story that he was sent away from the front line but he did not last long, not more than four or five days. I mean his presence at the front line.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And did he come back to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you in his company then?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. Yes, we were together one evening.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Zigic next?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I do. I know Zigic was arrested and taken into the detention unit in Banja Luka. And I think it had to do with his stay on the front line.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know when was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: It was in early July, and it lasted for about ten days.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you say that he was detained in Banja Luka, do you mean the district prison in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I mean the prison in Banja Luka at Tunjice.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when Zigic came out of prison, did you see him then?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes. I used to see him around Prijedor from time to time.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware of an incident which happened -- about the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 incident which happened in Prijedor between the 24th and 25th of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: You mean the Muslims who were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you in Keraterm at the time?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know if Zoran Zigic was in Keraterm at the time?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Zoran Zigic could not be in Keraterm at the time. He did not work there then.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How do you know that he wasn't in Keraterm that evening?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, he -- I was -- as a matter of fact, yes, that day, that day when it happened, I dropped by. I was trying to intercede on behalf of a friend or my former colleague, because we had to bury him. And I was passing by Keraterm, it was all blocked, and I could not get through to use the road which goes by Keraterm to Banja Luka so that I had to take another road. And I went around and I got to the Banja Luka road from the other side. I went to -- I approached men who were standing guard there because one could not pass Banja Luka road, and I did not see Zoran Zigic there, nor did I hear that he had been there that evening.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, did Zoran Zigic ever mention his kum and his uncle's kum, Hasan Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Once. I was present when he met his kum.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: It was at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: It was sometime in early August 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Before you went to Trnopolje, where did you see Zigic?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I saw Zoran Zigic in Bentley, which was a pizzeria, a well-known pizzeria in Prijedor and one of the few that were open, and we had coffee there together.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And did Zoran mention Trnopolje to you then?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Zoran said, "Come. Come with me. Let's go to together. I have to do something. I have to take something." I did not ask what or why. He asked me, "Will you come with me to Trnopolje?"

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know if he carried something with him on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: It was only when we got there that I saw that he had some food with him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know who was this food meant for?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes. It was meant for our friend, a very good guy from Prijedor called Cerka [phoen].

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And to whom was this food taken?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: The food was taken there for their parents, because his parents were ...

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when did you get to Trnopolje? When you arrived in Trnopolje, could you tell us whom did you see there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: When we arrived in Trnopolje -- we of course took the road, naturally, to the school. I think -- what was it? The school of something. It was the first time I'd been to Trnopolje. I'd never been there before. We parked the car. We got out of the car. "Come. Come. Come along. I have to hand something over." So we got out of the car. We started, we headed for the school or behind the school I - cannot remember exactly where - and a man approached, came to him. Then I heard that that was his kum. I don't know how, through his uncle or aunt. I can't really remember. And we had a rather heated conversation there because Zoran began to swear at his kum, something having to do with family matters, and shouting. And at some point he got him with his hand by the neck below the chin. It wasn't a blow really. It wasn't a scuffle or something. But that man, after that, that man whom he called kum, that Karabasic, he fell, because -- I mean I didn't know that man. I'd never seen him before. Then he said, "Come. Let's go. Forget this no good." And he took this food to the parents of that man that I mentioned before and said, "Let's go. Let's not stay here."

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was the food handed over to those people?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes. He personally handed it over.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What ethnic group to those people belong to?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: They were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, do you happen to know, during that particular month, whether Zoran Zigic was wounded again?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that too.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how you came to learn that and what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, I learnt it personally from the man who wounded him, who shot at him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Rajko Radic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you met him and how you came to hear of the occurrence?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I met him in town, but we knew each other from before the war, and he described what had happened. He said the following: He said that he shot at Zoran because Zoran came by in a car. He didn't want to stop. He had a machine-gun, a new machine-gun. It was all the an 84 machine-gun. And he shot at him, at the car. And I know that the son of -- Sikic's son was with him. He was underage, a boy underage. At the time, Zigic was wounded in the chin, and Rajko pointed, showed the red berry he had got and his sunglasses that he'd taken. He bragged about it. And at that time, many people were afraid of Zigic, so he bragged about having done this.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And my last question, Mr. President, and for you, Witness, could you describe what kind of man Zoran Zigic was? Briefly, please. What was he like before the war and what was he like during the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Before the war, he was a musician. He liked playing music when he was young, and he was always in love with music. He loved to play, and I think he still does today. He worked at the railway station and bus station as a taxi driver. That was his area. He was a normal man, an ordinary type of normal man. He had a wife and children, and he lived with them. And the time he spent in Prijedor, during that time I didn't hear much about him, anything special. He didn't make any trouble or anything of that kind. But when he returned from Pula, when he fled from Pula, I think that he was a different man. He drank. He drank a great deal, and he was quite a different man when he was sober and when he was drunk. He was a wonderful man and a gentleman when he was sober, but when he was drunk, he was dangerous, first of all to the people around him, for his friends. He drank a lot, as I say, and the difference was enormous, the kind of man he was before and the kind of man he was during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Deretic. Witness, you will now be answering questions put to you by the Prosecution unless any of the other Defence counsel wish to take the floor. No, they don't. So, Ms. Susan Somers, your witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I may, with two or three brief questions in private session that concern identification. Then I will proceed into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness, on the 29th of January of this year, do you recall --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On the 29th of January 2001 in Banja Luka, you met with investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not getting the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The answer was you did meet with investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor in Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I did meet with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And this was at your initiative. You contacted a person who you knew in a third country and through this third person, you requested to meet with these individuals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, as far as me personally. As far as I personally am concerned, I asked to meet with them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you requested to meet with them because you wanted to talk about the terrible things that you had done in the time period relevant to this indictment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. I wanted to meet with them to talk to them about it and to show that I personally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, I apologise for interrupting, but I think we must abstain from using this kind of language, "terrible things," the term you used, "terrible things that you had done." We are not here to judge this witness and he is not -- he does not stand accused, Ms. Susan Somers, so please try and be careful of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. I was paraphrasing from the language that the investigators had written through the individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure I understood your answer. To show that you personally what, what was the purpose of this meeting which you orchestrated?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: The subject was -- only had to do with me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what did you want to tell them? What did you personally want to relay to them?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: The same thing I'm telling you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which is your version of the facts or the version of the facts given to you by the lawyers for Mr. Zigic. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. It is according to my recollections and what I know about Keraterm during my stay there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You indicated to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor that you wanted to talk with a lawyer. You indicated you did talk with a lawyer, that it was one of Zigic's lawyers, and you preferred to talk to the investigators without a lawyer present. Which of Zigic's lawyers did you talk to, was it Stojanovic, Deretic, or someone else?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: When do you mean actually?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Prior to meeting with the investigators in January, on the 29th of January 2001 in Banja Luka. You specifically indicated to them that you wanted to talk to a lawyer. You indicated it was one of Zigic's lawyers, which one was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I did not talk to Zigic's lawyers before that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the course of that meeting, you were asked, after having been cautioned in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, you gave certain responses to certain questions. Did you bring with you and did you show to counsel for Mr. Zigic the video cassette, the video recording of the cautioned interview of the 29th of January?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, I didn't show it to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is it still in your possession?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, I threw the cassette away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You indicated that the time period, you were asked about your time period in Keraterm, and you suggested that you were there for a period of I believe you said seven days; would that have been correct? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, I spent four shifts, perhaps five shifts. I can't remember exactly. I have already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Well, which days -- on which days would you put those shifts? I think you could possibly help us understand your situation better if you explained the days you told the investigators you were in Keraterm. Could you please be very specific, the month and the day?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: In June, the 4th of June, the 6th of June, because we worked 24 hours. We were on duty 24 hours so I had a day off and I worked a day. The 4th of June, the 6th of June, I think that's when it was or possibly -- no, that's not possible. The 4th of June, the 6th of June, the 8th of June, the 10th of June, the 12th. Now, as for the sixth shift, I'm not quite sure. I think that the sixth time, I went to Zivko Knezevic to report to him and that I was relieved of my duties then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So when do you actually take yourself out of Keraterm camp? When have you finished whatever duties you claim to have been assigned at Keraterm camp, your last official day?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I think that my last official day was the 12th. And on the 13th or 14th, I went to report to Zivko. Perhaps I stopped by Keraterm to take my weapons and to give everything back and sign off so to speak. That was that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your relationship with [redacted] a blood relative or relative by marriage?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecutor gives her own qualifications, things that the witness never said. The witness never mentioned [redacted]. He never said that. Therefore, my learned colleague's question stems from the fact that [redacted]. It is a leading question drawing conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, would you ask whether he [redacted] and carry on after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Gladly Your Honour, and the basis for it was the acknowledgment that was in private session which would have put him squarely with the knowledge of positions. So in effect, the Chamber has heard this witness acknowledge that he was the person to whom I referred to in private session. I think that would indicate how he would know the relationship. In accordance with the Chamber's direction, do you know an individual named, I believe, [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And his relationship to you by blood or marriage was? How are you related, please?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: His role in Keraterm was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm wondering, this question and answer, does it disclose the identity of the witness or does it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, perhaps. Ms. Susan Somers --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In which case, Your Honour, may I request an appropriate redaction for -- or if the Chamber would redact and allow me to go into private session to rephrase my question or simply redact accordingly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Madam Registrar, may we have that portion redacted and let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are we in private session yet?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness DD/9, your understanding of the role of Dusan Sikirica in Keraterm was what?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I didn't think he did anything. I didn't know what he did there. While he was in Keraterm, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness, I will read to you something that has been subject to a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 revised translation being submitted, brought before this Chamber. It is Prosecution 3/249. It is an official note of 4 July 1992, compiled by Dusko Sikirica, with the title "Commander of Keraterm Security." Is that the role that you understood Sikirica to hold in Keraterm, Commander of security?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: They could have called him whatever they liked. I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where was your home in relationship to the home of Sikirica, the dwelling in which you stayed?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: About let us say 700 metres, give or take a hundred metres, between our houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And were you in -- on the territory of the municipality -- I'm giving you a broad municipality orientation. Were you on the territory of Prijedor throughout the months of May through the end of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes. I was born there and that's where I still live.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And do you know if Dusko Sikirica was also on the territory of Prijedor municipality during that time period?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the note --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I can't say exactly the period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the note which I have just made reference to from 4 July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, I apologise for interrupting you, but it is you now who are leading the witness in a sense. You asked, if you look at the transcript and at line 19, page 59, line 19, your question was how the witness understood the task this person was performing, and his answer was that he didn't know whether he did anything. "I don't know because he was there and I was not there." And now you're reading a document and you're saying, "Is that how you understood it?" The witness said he didn't understand anything by it. So would you put that as being a leading question, Ms. Susan Somers? If the witness answers, "I don't know. I didn't understand anything," et cetera, et cetera, you go on to read a document and then you're saying, "Is that what you understood it?" Please proceed, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My question was in the understanding of the title that was read as opposed -- if it was consonant with any understanding he may or may not have had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but it was the title that you asked previously. But continue with what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know a person named Zoran Vokic?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I did do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know a person named Zeljko Timarac?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You indicated you knew a person named Dusko Knezevic and that you knew the a person -- the accused Zoran Zigic. I ask this as these are the four names referred to as being -- as having been subjected to warnings by Sikirica not to come into Keraterm. Would there be any reason in your mind, if you might have any thoughts, why your name would also not be included in that list of persons not to come into Keraterm? If you know, answer. If you don't, tell us that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again, this is a leading question, a question which contains an answer to it. The witness has said nothing. I didn't hear the answer. I didn't hear him say whether he knew about this order, conclusion, or whatever it was. I think I heard that properly. So in that context, I should like to request that my learned colleague restate her question or to ask questions and lead up to the topic in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think perhaps it would be better if I read that passage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the document referred to, Prosecutor's 3/249, signed by -- purporting to have been signed by Dusko Sikirica as Commander of Keraterm, there is a passage which reads: "Zoran, son of Nikola Zigic, an armed uniform person (I do not know which unit he belongs to) came to the Keraterm reception centre several times at night together with Dusko Knezevic, Zoran Vokic, and Zeljko Timarac. Despite our warnings not to enter the compound, they entered, explaining that they were going to talk to one of the prisoners." My question - and you may or may not know the answer, and if you don't, please so indicate - is: Why was your name not included in that list of persons not to enter Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, I don't know whether the witness knows about this document. The question has been put in an abstract manner, just as if he were asked whether he knew that it -- whether it would snow in five minutes' time. Please, I should like to have more specific questions asked and not to have questions contain answers that are expected of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, does the witness know about this document? Has he identified it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It has not been put to the witness as a document. He does not have it in front of him which is why I'm asking him if he can relate or give some comment on particular parts having given evidence of his relationship to Zigic. I ask for nothing more than if he has no answer, just to so indicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness, you have indicated in your direct examination that you tracked fairly closely the activities or at least the comings and goings of Zoran Zigic and you made reference to his having lost his position. If, in fact, one can look at this document as relating to your comment about having lost the position and about access to the camp, my question is: Why is your name not on this list or do you find yourself not associated with the group of people I so mentioned?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Witness. Your comment about Zigic's having left Keraterm, what was your understanding of the reasons for his departure from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He could go when he liked. He could leave Keraterm when he liked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Could you? Could you leave Keraterm when you liked?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know the relationship, if any, of accused Zigic to a police official by the same last name? A police official named Zigic. Do you know the relationship of Zoran Zigic to that police official. I believe the first name may have been Rajko.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I think they were originally from the same village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are they related?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was that person --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of relationship. Probably they were related. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know what position Rajko Zigic occupied, let's say from May to August of 1992 in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Whose position? Could you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to help the Chamber and the Prosecution, that man died some time in the 1980s.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did that individual die, if you know exactly?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I do not know exactly when that person died, but his brother, Rajko Zigic's brother, is a neighbour of mine so I can ask him and then let you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was he also a police official, the brother?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. No, he wasn't a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When -- you made reference in your taped interview with the Office of the Prosecutor investigators in Banja Luka to the "late Zivko Knezevic." When did Zivko Knezevic die?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: In the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What month?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. Perhaps it was August. I'm not -- I am not saying exactly because I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was he still at Keraterm when you supposedly left Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Mr. Zivko Knezevic was the Commander of the police station Prijedor 2 at Urije.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was he still exerting his authority over Keraterm at the time you were in Keraterm and when you left Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How did he die?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Natural causes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which were?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When you were in Keraterm, who was the shift leader under whom you worked?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Specifically on my shift, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You worked without any type of person supervising you; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: That's right. No orders. None of us were -- none of us had a rank. None of us was in a position to issue orders to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In your interview by the Office of the Prosecutor investigators in Banja Luka, you were asked to explain who was in charge of shifts and your response was: "So this means there were two shifts only while I was there. And there were two bosses of the shifts too, chiefs of the shifts. There was the boss of my shift and the boss of the other shift." And you were asked, "Can you give the names of the bosses of the shift?" And you answered, "I think the chief my shift was Kolundzija at the time. He's in The Hague. I don't know, maybe in the other shift. Yes, he was in mine. He was in my shift."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, we are in Keraterm. What does it have to do with Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did I say Omarska? I meant Keraterm. If I slipped, it was Keraterm. If Omarska is in the record, the reference was, at all times, was to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. No. That is my question. That is my question. You are unfolding this question about those people who were the shift leaders in Keraterm, and I am asking you what does it have to do with the case before us?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Some of the charges, certainly a number of the Zigic charges are Keraterm-based charges and it tests the credibility of this witness. He has given a diametrically opposed answer in the Chamber today to what he gave to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, go ahead. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What -- now which is it? Did you have a shift commander such as Kolundzija or did you not? Which will you stick by?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, he wasn't my shift leader. He wasn't my shift leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So you lied to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why did you throw out the video of your interview? What prompted you to do that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, that tape is worthless to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Because it's full of lies; is that why?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. No. But because the investigators induced me to tell them other stories, and those interviews had nothing to do with me. And once they started, and then I interrupted my interview with them. I refused to talk to them anymore because, as I said, they were trying to take me along some other trail which I -- trying to induce me to talk about something else and at that time, I wasn't under oath either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In the beginning of that interview, you were told by the investigator leading the interview after he identified himself, "You are a suspect of committing, you may have committed a crime on which the Tribunal has jurisdiction. Specifically, we are investigating criminal acts which you may have committed personally at Keraterm camp in 1992. As a suspect, you have certain rights. You are entitled to be informed of your rights in a language you understand, and have the free assistance of an interpreter. You understand what the interpreter says to you?" Your answer, "Yes." The investigator: "You have the right to remain silent which means you do not have to answer my questions. Do you understand that?" Your answer: "Yes. Yes." The investigator: "If you answer any question or if you speak to me at all, anything you say may be used as evidence against you in trial at any criminal proceeding. Do you understand that?" Your answer: "Yes, I understand." If you decide -- the investigator: "If you decide to answer my questions, everything we say will be audio-video recorded. I am recording the advice which I am giving you now. Recording of any statement you or can you use as evidence against you in any criminal proceeding." Your response: "Yes, it's clear to me." Investigator: "You have the right to be assisted by a lawyer. If you cannot afford to hire a lawyer, the Tribunal will appoint a lawyer to represent you before any questioning takes place, if you wish. This will be done without any expense to you. Do you understand this?" Your answer: "I understand." "If you decide to answer my questions now without a lawyer present," that's the investigator --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The investigator then said: "If you decide to answer my questions now without a lawyer present, you have the right at any time during my questioning to stop answering questions until you've had the opportunity to consult with a lawyer. Do you understand that?" Your answer: "I understand." The investigator: "Having just been informed of your rights, do you wish now to talk to me and answer my questions?" Your answer: "Yes." Now, I would like to ask a little bit about some of the different persons who may have come to Keraterm while you were there. Do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, what was the question? I did not understand. What did you want to ask before all this? What was your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was a response to the comment about induced answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What I have just read to you is a verbatim rendition of the discussion between you and the investigator. Is this what you call induced questioning or induced discussion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Give us -- let's hear your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, because my learned friend first dictated for the record all that she thought should be included, and before that the witness had already answered how did the interview unfold, that he at some point refused to answer questions and then interrupted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Deretic, but the Prosecutor demonstrated in which way the interview unfolded. So where is the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem because the witness has already said. He said that, "At the moment the investigators began to induce me to give them the answer they wanted to hear, I interrupted the interview."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes. Right. Very well. Ask your question, Ms. Somers. Objection is rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you: Is this what you call an inducement?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The rights -- the questions and answers concerning the various rights which you enjoy under the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal that were read to you and which you responded to, that have just been made part of this record, do you consider anything that would have been said afterward, after you agreed to talk to the investigator, do you consider anything said an inducement after having been given all those cautions?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Let me tell you, madam, to begin with, I had this interview at the SFOR base where I did indeed surrender, but I thought that these interviews would have to do with me personally and nobody else, none of the accused here. That is why I think that -- that is why I said they were inducing me, and it was for those reasons that I put an end to that interview. I left the base and went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At the end of that interview, the supervisory investigator, having suspected that you were not telling the truth, confirmed by saying, "I want to clear a few things first. You asked for this meeting; is that correct?" Your answer: "It is to tell you like this." And I will omit the name so as not to endanger the third party. "The third party, maybe he did not relay this to you as he should have done. I am for a conversation. Before the direct accusation of someone, no. We did not speak about that. When he and I spoke, he wanted to help me." Why did you really contact the Office of the Prosecutor? Was it to give up other people? Was it to have a social discussion? What was the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: What I wanted was my case, specifically my case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you wish to be indicted? Is that what you wanted?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. I wanted to be relieved of all those charges.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did you understand there to be charges pending at that time or did you just want to confess?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. No. I wanted to be exonerated, because I knew that that indictment was frozen. I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Well, if you wanted to have an exoneration, you were asked if you knew anything about somebody named Drago Tokmadzic. Your answer: "Yes, I've heard of him."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you hear about him?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I hear that he's dead. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you see him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but I read one statement from The Hague that he was dead. I don't know exactly who, what's his name, you see, the guy accused of that, but I also mentioned my name. In fact, your name was mentioned in testimony before The Hague and that was in the testimony of (redacted) who squarely put you as one of the individuals responsible for the death of Tokmadzic. How did you wish to exonerate yourself if you deny any involvement, just by saying, "No. I only heard that he was dead"? Explain, please.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I simply don't know how to answer this question, because I did -- I neither participated in the murder of Drago Tokmadzic, nor did I take part in the beating up of Edin Ganic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Well, then, how did you find out about the beating of Ganic?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: From you, as of today. And I also heard some stories. I don't know exactly. Yes, I heard some stories that there had been some statements. Not hundred per cent, but it is as of today. Today, from Mr. Deretic and from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did Mr. Deretic tell you and when did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise, Witness. My microphone was not on. What did Mr. Deretic tell you and when did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: What do you mean what Mr. Deretic had told me?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You said you heard about (redacted), in part through -- you claim me, although I fail to find any reference to his beating up in the record made by me, but what did you hear from Mr. Deretic about it and when did you hear it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Right now. Just now. You mentioned it yourself, and about half an hour, an hour ago, it was Mr. Deretic who brought it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In order to have your name cleared, were you prepared to talk about the death of Car, a person named Car, with the investigators? Do you recall your comments about that death?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, he was beaten. He was battered.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And how did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I was in the camp then. I worked in the camp at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you were asked by the investigator: "Okay. There was a prisoner. His nickname was Car. Did you know hear that name or know that person? You answered: "Yes, I know."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I heard that Duca killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: From whom did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: From Srdja.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who's that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: From the guards. From the other guards. What were you doing while Car was being beaten and ultimately beaten to the point of being killed? What were you doing in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Madam, I did not want to discuss Car's murder with the investigators then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection again. The Prosecutor is asking a question to which the witness has already answered, "What were you doing at the time," meaning while Car was there. And the witness has described in detail day four and day six when he was there and saw what happened to Car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question was: "What were" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps you should word it more precisely, because otherwise Mr. Deretic will be right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to perhaps backtrack and say, "Why did you not want to discuss the Car matter with the investigators," and then I would ask the Chamber afterward for a moment of private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why did you want to discuss this matter with the investigators?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I've answered this question five times, ma'am, and I came here because of my own case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May we go into private session for just a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You were also unwilling to discuss what you may or may not have known about other persons involved in the death of Car; why is that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I did not want to discuss it. I have already answered this question, and repeatedly so, because this whole interview was to be about me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was it about you that you wanted to discuss?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: About my indictment, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What concerned you about it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, not much. I didn't give -- it didn't give me much concern, the indictment, or else I wouldn't have been talking to the investigators in the SFOR base. I do not know what is in my indictment specifically, I simply don't. But -- you understand what I'm trying to tell you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You went to the SFOR base with the investigators from the Office of the Prosecution in a UN-marked vehicle. You did not hide, did you, at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. No. I did not hide.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was it about an indictment that you say concerns you that you wanted to discuss with the investigators? It is not clear from any of your answers, and please try to help us understand what the purpose of your setting up the meeting was.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know what is in my indictment. I do not see my indictment, and I do not exactly know what's in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This may require private session to clarify this. It is very confusing to me what is being referred to perhaps we should -- if the Chamber is minded to pick this up after lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Perhaps this is a convenient time to adjourn and we shall resume in 50 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Ms. Susan Somers, how much more time do you need to finish the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to take my full time, Your Honour. I believe my colleague has indicated I have approximately 30-ish minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, you're there, I see. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I can hear you, but can I ask you something? May I ask something, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I should like to ask us to wind up this in a proper manner and that all the questions that you put to me, that they refer in concrete terms to Zoran Zigic, because I am a witness here for Zoran Zigic, and I don't want you to tie me with the other questions. This will facilitate me in answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. That was the object of my own preoccupations as well. I would like to remind you that as witness, you can refuse to make any declarations which could incriminate you, to say anything that could incriminate you. The Chamber can make you answer questions, and that is our Rule. It is Rule 90 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And the Rule also says -- yes, it may happen that you can incriminate yourself, but you can respond and say that in a situation like this, the testimony cannot be used as an element of proof against you except in the case -- for any offence other than false testimony. "Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." So you may be answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor. If you feel that the answer can incriminate you, you can tell us. The Chamber can compel you to answer, but in that case, your response, your answers can never be used against you, in a subsequent prosecution against you as evidence. Does that deal with your worries, Witness? Has that put your mind at rest, Witness?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I'm ready to continue testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Witness. Ms. Susan Somers, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness DD/9, you had indicated in your direct testimony that because of your failure to comply with rules in Keraterm, you had to leave. Can you please tell us specifically which rules in Keraterm you failed to comply with?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, spending 24 hours in Keraterm, for example, going at my own free will, things like that. There were others too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which others?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I didn't regularly take up my guard duties at my guard post. I went when I wanted to. I came back when I felt like it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who took over your guard post if you abandoned it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know, madam, exactly. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who set these rules or who made these rules and who enforced these rules?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: You mean the rules governing our stay in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The rules that you said you failed to comply with. Who made them and who enforced them?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, the rules and our stay in Keraterm was determined by Zivko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who was just a police chief in Urije; is that correct? Nothing more than a police chief in Urije?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes. Keraterm is on the territory of Urije, Urije, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And who enforced these rules if there were a violation as you say you committed?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, for example, I did. I went against the rules and I was sent away by Mr. Zivko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So it was Zivko Knezevic who made the rules and your testimony was it was Zivko Knezevic, who is dead, who enforced the rules; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know whether he made the rules, but in my particular case, he enforced that rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, I think that we have lost our connection. No, the witness is there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you ever disciplined by Dusko Sikirica?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I had no contact with Dusko Sikirica in Keraterm at all because he came after I had left. I don't know how many days after exactly, but we weren't there at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, why that question? Why that question? The witness has already said that he was in Keraterm, and after he had left, that Sikirica arrived. So I don't understand why you're asking that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not accept the dates that this witness is giving for his stay in Keraterm and I will proceed to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You told -- you were asked by the investigator in the interview in Banja Luka between yourself and the Office of the Prosecutor, you were asked, did -- if you had taken part in beatings. And your answer was, "I personally did not."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The questioning continued during the examination where he said, "During the time you were being beaten, were any of these individuals asking you questions or saying things to you [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: quotation, Your Honours, from the transcript, "I don't like saying this in front of the Court but I have to ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be better --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Can we repeat all that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be better to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think that -- it would be appropriate for just a few minutes to go into private session, and if there is any redaction I would request it be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, redactions will have to be made. Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really am no longer certain whether this misspeaking is intentional when my learned colleague is reading and mentioning the name of a protected witness. And in my profound opinion, we have seen the process. We know that the witness is a sick man. He has come to testify with a high temperature and that is why he didn't -- he came because the previous witness didn't come. So would the Prosecution bear that in mind. He is a sick man at present, and what I said before. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I'm going to ask Ms. Susan Somers to pay attention and take great care. We are all doing this. We are doing our utmost, and so we need not bring up the matter of intentional. You too, Mr. Deretic, have made slips. But may I ask you, Ms. Susan Somers, to please be careful. Take care. Because as you know, it is very difficult to remedy the situation once a mistake has occurred. So please try and pay attention to the text that you're going to read out, the questions you are going to ask, to know whether you need to go into private session to read it or to ask your questions. If you are going to need it, I'm going to give you five extra minutes for you to go back and study your material. Do you need the extra five minutes to see what you need to do?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I would request, and I do apologise to Chamber, to counsel, and the witness for an unintentional slip. I would ask for private session for a few minutes. I think it will facilitate the next line of questioning without any terrible worry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but please be careful in future. Please proceed. Let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Ms. Somers. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Witness DD/9, was Zoran Zigic made to leave Keraterm as you indicated he was?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He didn't have to leave Keraterm. He would leave Keraterm whenever he felt like it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want to make sure I understand that you did -- you stated you did not socialise with Zoran Zigic, but you indicated you knew he had bandages on for some two to two and a half months, also indicating that he had left Keraterm. How did you know that he had bandages on for two to two and a half months which would have, by your reckoning, taken us into end of June, perhaps July. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Madam, I went out into coffee bars. We frequented the same coffee bars. He went where I did. I didn't see him every day, but we would bump into each other. He was a neighbour of mine. We would sometimes exchange a few words and sit down to have a drink together. So that's how I knew. I knew more or less at least as far as his health was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You mentioned a machine-gun, I believe near the weighing hut or booth and you described it as "old". By describing it as old, were you suggesting it was not operational?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't really know whether it worked or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You also described the weapon with which Car was made to run around after it had been emptied of ammunition as old. Was it your understanding that there was a concern that while it was old, it was operational, the weapon that Car had?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: The machine-gun was of the same type.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And it had ammunition that was taken from it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: The ammunition was taken out of the machine-gun when Car was brought to Keraterm, and the weapon could have functioned. I wasn't armed. Car was armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: During the time you were in Keraterm, did you observe any doctors coming to take care of Emsud Bahonjic, or Drago Tokmadzic, or Car? Did anyone come to render medical assistance in Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: As far as Car is concerned, when I left at 6.00 in the morning, when I left my shift, when I went off duty, at that particular time, around about that time, somebody called, I don't know who exactly, and a doctor came, and a policeman came --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who was the doctor?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: -- to establish death.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Who was the doctor, the name?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But the doctor only came to establish --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But your testimony is the doctor came only to establish death not to assist in sustaining life; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Ms. Somers. Mr. Deretic, do you have any additional questions on re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only two short ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness, from this machine-gun which was placed in that machine-gun nest, was it ever fired while you were there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, and we didn't know whether it was in operational order or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And my second question: When I asked you about Ramadanovic nicknamed Sengin, whether he had been taken to the hospital, you had answered in the affirmative. Do you know if people were taken to the hospital to receive treatment or to be killed?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: They were taken to the hospital to receive treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Deretic. Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness DD/9, good afternoon. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just also have perhaps one or two questions to ask you. You mentioned that Mr. Zigic, the only assignment of Mr. Zigic was to carry food and water. You said that perhaps was his only assignment. How do you know it was his only assignment?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Because that's all he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And how do you know it was all he did? Were you with him all the time?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I have already said that Mr. Zigic came and went. We couldn't be together in Keraterm all the time, and during those times which I know when I was there, when he was there, that those are the only times that I can describe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said also that he only worked in the day and never came to the camp at night. Were you at the camp at night?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, yes, for a few hours, because we changed. Some people went home to sleep for two or three hours, and other guys would come in. So we rotated. We were never all together in Keraterm. We were never all in one shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But usually --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: In one and the same shift.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I remember you saying you went home.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Sir, I did not say that I went home at night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You were not there at night, were you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I did not say that I was not there at night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were you there at night? Would you spend the nights there? That's my question. And were you awake to know who is coming and who is going?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't be -- I wouldn't spend there the whole night, and at times I'd sleep. I'd snatch two or three hours of sleep or two or three hours I would spend walking around, and at times I also went home to get some two or three hours of sleep too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Zigic could leave the Keraterm camp whenever he liked. Do you mean by that he did not need to take anybody's permission? He was his own master.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: You will have to repeat this question to me, sir, because I am having interruptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said Mr. Zigic could leave the --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Can you hear me now? Can you?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Zigic could leave the camp whenever he liked. Do you mean by that he did not need anybody's permission, that he was master of all his actions and he had no boss?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He did not have a boss in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. You mentioned that he -- he is the one who ordered that Car would go around with a machine-gun and run around. So did he have some kind of superior role where he can give orders?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. He was drunk on that occasion. He was shouting at everybody, screaming. He did not issue orders to the man to carry around this machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Didn't he order that Car would run around with the machine-gun, and then he went away after a quarter of an hour?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, he made him carry that machine-gun around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Could any guard or simple soldier do that, order anything around?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You just mentioned that when he is drunk, that he was almost -- there was some kind of a -- of duality in him. He was a gentleman when he was sober, and he was dangerous when he was drunk even to his friends. What would it be when he was in the camp? Was he also dangerous to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: You know what, sir, he would at times go in, start kissing and hugging the prisoners, offer them cigarettes or give them whole packages, and at other times he'd swear at them and abuse them, and that's the same way how he treated me. Not only me but all his other friends too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Riad. Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness DD/9, you told us that Mr. Sikirica didn't come to Keraterm until after you had left. During the period that you were a guard at Keraterm, who was the top boss in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Mr. Zivko Knezevic, the deceased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Did he have anybody who was like number 2, who took over when he slept or when he had to leave the camp?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He wasn't in the camp. He was at the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Was anybody in charge of the camp when he wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I suppose those in the police might know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Now, while you were a guard at Keraterm, could you and the other guards come to the camp and leave the camp? Could you get into the camp and out of the camp whenever you wanted to or could you only be allowed to enter the camp when you were on your duty shift? If you don't understand, I'll repeat the question. In other words, if you were a guard there, could you only come into the camp during your shift or could you come in at other times?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Only during our own shift. We were there only when our shift was on duty. All the rest of the time, we would have a rest because it was very hard work. It was 24 hours. You understand what I mean. It was hard work. It was a long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: No. I understand that. But for instance, if you worked the night-shift on the camp and sometime during the day you wanted to come in for some reason, to visit another guard, to talk to a detainee, could you come into the camp? Would the people on the -- you know, at the guard post at the access to the camp let you though? They'd know you were a guard. Would they let you in even though it wasn't your shift? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I don't know, because I didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And the one reason I asked is I thought you mentioned at one point - and I'll go back and check to make sure I'm not mistaken - that Mr. Zigic sometimes came, appeared or left on his moped. It sounds as though a person could come in and go out even though it wasn't his shift if he was a regular guard at some point.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: That's only how it sounded to you. I don't know. I don't know what you meant by this. We were together. We were on the same shift. Did he come and go then? About the rest, I don't know, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned that he had a bandaged hand during a period -- during one period and held it up and complained about the pain in his hand, is that right, after his index finger was --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe you said right after he left the camp, right after you and he left Keraterm, he was taken to the front or he was ordered to the front; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. He first spent several days in hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: After he left Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: What is not correct?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He spent in the hospital several days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: After he left Keraterm? I'm just trying to get the time lines here correct. When he left Keraterm, was his finger bandaged?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes. His finger was bandaged and there were complications even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Are you now -- I just want to get it straight. Are you now saying that after you and he left Keraterm, I thought you said - perhaps I was wrong - I though you said that he then went to the front for several days, but are you saying that after he left Keraterm, he went back to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: When he left Keraterm, he went to the hospital and spent several days there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. My last question is -- well, there are two actually. You were asked about whether or not you knew that on a certain night there were many deaths of Muslims in Keraterm, and you said you heard about it, and I believe you -- and then you were asked whether you knew whether or not Zigic was there, and you said well, it so happened that you had to go by the camp and it was lit up and there were lots of soldiers around, but you didn't see Zigic there. I think that's what you said. Is that right? You just said you didn't see him there on the night when you passed by the camp when there were these deaths of Muslims there. My only question to you - it isn't very detailed - is: Can you repeat for me when that night was, approximately when that night was? Because I have two -- two different times down in my notes, and I just want to know what you are saying, when that occurred.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Madam, to begin with, it was night-time. I didn't go anywhere at night. It was the next day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: So that is the answer to one of your questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, I stand corrected, and I thank you for that. Now, I simply want to know what date that was.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Well, now, if I had a telephone here, I could tell you, because that night -- that night I spent at my friends' because their brother had been killed, and I cannot give you the exact date now. Perhaps I can let you know later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's all right. Can you tell me the month? Can you just tell me the month?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'll go wrong, so, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, you told us earlier in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I think it was June. June. June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's good enough. And my last question --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: June. June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My last question to you is in relation to your answer to Judge Riad's question about how Mr. Zigic was kind to the prisoners when he was sober and at other times you said he abused them. Would you just tell us what kind of abuse you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I did not say that Mr. Zigic ill-treated Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: It came through on the monitor, unless there is some error in the translation, "At other times he abused them." If that's wrong, you can say so. I'm just quoting from the way it appeared on the English translation monitor.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Please may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you repeat this, because there are interruptions in the link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes, I will. In answer to Judge Riad's question, you said that when Mr. Zigic was sober, many times he was kind to the prisoners, gave them things, and that at other times, presumably when he had too much alcohol, he abused them. Now, the word "abuse" came through in the English translation. I just wanted to know what you meant by "abuse" when you used it. If you didn't use it and the translation is wrong, you can say that.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: That is a misinterpretation. I've already answered this question. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I can also deny an answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm going to insist that you give me an answer to that question, because I simply -- since the term appeared, I simply want to know -- you can say anything you want in answer to that.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: There are interruptions again. We are having interruptions all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. Let me put it this way so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: There are interruptions here. Now it's fine. Now it seems to be working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it to make it easier for you. You did tell us that when -- many times Mr. Zigic was very kind to the prisoners, did you not?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You said at other times he was not. I heard you use the word translated to be "abused," but just tell us how he acted toward the prisoners on those other times.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Sometimes when he was drunk, he would sometimes go to prisoners, hug them, kiss them, distribute cigarettes. When he was drunk he also gave them cigarettes and hugged them, but he also cursed them, swore at their mothers, and he was angry and indignant, but he treated us the same as he treated those Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. So your answer is --

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He would also swear at us and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: He would curse or swear at them, is that right, at these other times?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: But he also insulted us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. I also have a few short questions. I should like to -- I understood that you answered Mr. Deretic -- you were asked if you knew Mr. Emsud Bahonjic, and I believe that you answered that you didn't, that you had only heard that man's name mentioned on one occasion. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what did you hear said about this man?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I only heard about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But what is it that you heard about him?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Nothing specific. Nothing to pin down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Witness, I must insist on this. What is it that you heard? It is for me to determine whether something is specific or not. My question is: What did you hear being said about that man?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
