utterances.text: I heard that name mentioned in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So your answer to my question is "I merely heard his name"; is that it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Another question, Witness. We spoke here, I do not know whether we used the term, but we did refer to a massacre in Keraterm, even if we did not use that word. Do you know what we are referring to?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the date for me? What was the date when that incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact date right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I should repeat the question and I'll do that, but do you remember the year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the month?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I think it was July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You think that it was July. And the date?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Mr. President, I could give you the date if I only could call the family of this friend of mine with whom I spent that evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see, but I am asking you. If your answer is "I do not know," then why don't you tell me, "I do not know."

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Fine. But you are telling me that it was in 1992 and that it was July; is that it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Another question. I should like to invite you to think back to the incident when the doctor came to certify the death, a death. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. How do you know that it was a physician, a doctor?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: He was wearing a white frock and he had a policeman with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You say, "He was." You are sure that it was a man, that it was a male doctor?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was a man; is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Couldn't it have been a nurse?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Sir, I do not know what he was because I do not know what kind of authority he had. I -- that morning, I went home. I did not linger there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. Then why do you say that that doctor came to certify a death? How do you know that that was the reason he came, to certify a death?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: That's what I heard. I heard that a doctor had come. He walked past me, he and a policeman, and they went in the direction of Car. So as I was coming out, I said, "What's this?" And they said, "Well, it seems a doctor had come to certify a death."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Very well. Do you remember the time -- which time of the day was it more or less?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Early in the morning, because I left normally at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this happened before or as you were leaving, that is, it was before 6.00, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: No. We met as I was coming out, as I was leaving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So one can say at 6.00, more or less, because as you were leaving, the doctor was coming in.

utterances.speaker: Witness DD/9
utterances.text: Yes, a man in a white -- yes, dressed in white, and a policeman. Yes, they were coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Very well. Well, Witness, we have no further questions for you. Thank you very much for coming, and we wish you success in your work. I believe we have a question -- a matter to resolve here, but it will be -- but you are free to go now, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I see Mr. Deretic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in relation to the testimony of this witness, Mr. Zigic's Defence would like to suggest and give to the Chamber, to our learned friends of the Prosecution, and my other friends in the Defence a document. So I would like to ask the usher to help us, and the document has to do with the time frame which Mr. Zigic spent in the gaol at Tunjice near Banja Luka. And we should like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam registrar, could you give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it is D20/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there was also another document which we needed to discuss, madam registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. That one was already identified as D19/4. It was actually submitted the week before last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the transcript is wrong. It says D24/4, that is, slash nothing. Line 16.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, it is D 20/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think we've got the number right now. Mr. Deretic, there are two things here which we need to discuss and we have to organise this discussion well so as to finish, and we also have to give Ms. Somers time to answer. We are -- you are therefore tendering this document D20/4. Will you tell us the reason -- will you lay the foundation for this, the document, and we also have a document which we half discussed in the middle of the examination-in-chief. Is it not the same document, the document which has already been registered and admitted at the number of which is D19/4? So these are the two questions that we need to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I do not think it is one and the same document, that is, the document which I have as registered 19/4 is a document which has to do with the document, that is, it is the fragment from the -- excerpt from the criminal record of persons mentioned here today who were detainees in the investigation centre at Keraterm. The document marked 20/4, D20/4 and the original which I have before me is a document which was issued by the Banja Luka penitentiary and which shows that between the 1st and the 9th of July 1992, Zoran Zigic was a detainee there. So these are two different documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is a problem -- no, I don't think it's the problem of interpretation but understanding. Mr. Deretic, will you tell me if the document that you produced in the middle of the examination of the witness is the document which was marked D19/4? And you did not answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. President, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my next question is: Why do you -- are asking for the admission of the document which is already in the file?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it was pending your ruling. Because the Prosecution objected, and the Chamber was to rule on this because the Prosecution objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait. Wait. Madam Registrar, will you please show these two documents to Mr. Deretic? Or the usher, will you please do that? So, Mr. Deretic, do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Mr. President, but this is the first time that I hear that this document was admitted. I suggested to use it as an exhibit, and when I did that, I understood that the Chamber would rule upon it at a later date because it was -- because I made this -- I produced the document after the examination of Witness DD/5. So there was only my good intention behind it, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I do think we have a problem. Let us try to resolve it. The Chamber tells you that 9 -- no. This is the same thing. On the 10th of April, in the record, on the transcript, 9999 - there are four 9s, 9999 - you have the decision of the Chamber which decided to admit this document, D19/4, which is exactly the same document whose admission you are seeking today. So my question is do you want one and the same document admitted twice or do we admit it only once?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Mr. President. All I had in mind, and evidently it is my fault, my impression was the document had not been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But the document has been admitted already. It is D19/4. The decision of the Chamber on the page -- on the LiveNote, on the page that I have already indicated. There is no need to waste any more time discussing that document, because this exhibit -- I believe that Judge Wald, however, wishes to comment on this document or its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I recollect that it was admitted. At that time I made a statement saying I didn't think it was relevant, but it was admitted at that time. So if it's admitted, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There was this -- there was this caveat. The Chamber do not -- does not think that this document is of high relevance. We do not really see any major relevance, but the Chamber will be weighing these exhibits among other evidence, manage other exhibits, but it is being admitted. Now, Ms. Somers, I do not know if you wish to say something else with regard to this document, D19/4. I do not think -- I think that it has been -- that it is an admitted exhibit and that you wish to say something with regard to document D20/4, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On 19/4, Your Honour, you're correct. I must admit I had to think through again, because I remember making the very same arguments, but only now when you bring it up, and of course our objection is a record objection and continues. On 20/4, what Mr. Deretic is effectively doing is at this stage in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 the trial injecting a new alibi of which we have had no notice and to which we object. There is no witness competent to have presented this through unless he could have done it through the witness who just left, but this is a totally inappropriate document for purposes of this stage of the process. There's effectively taking Zigic out of Keraterm, claiming to do so, and we object to it. It is not timely. I think it is error to admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it was the Prosecutor who encouraged me to do this, because the Prosecutor used the document from which we learned about the time frame to which the Prosecutor referred, and I do not think that this document was tendered in this case. So I merely checked in the relevant penitentiary and really saw that indeed from the -- that Zoran Zigic was detained there between the 1st and the 9th of July, and I found official confirmation for this now, since the Prosecutor produced here a photocopy of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: For whatever enlightenment it may cast on the subject, I don't have the transcript, but my notes say that the witness we have just heard, whose name I won't repeat here, but that he testified that Mr. Zigic went to the front lines at a certain point and then said he was later arrested in early July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I respond, Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In which case I think this should have been put to the witness. I think to stick it in without any type of ability to discuss the document is inappropriate, but again it is an element of alibi that is inappropriate to raise at this time. May I add that if we have to present further evidence to meet this newly injected alibi, then we would ask, of course, that it be taken off the time of the Defence during its rebuttal if need be. I will have to examine. This is completely new.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Deretic, let me ask you a question if I may. Rule 67, which talks about the defence of alibi, and as you know -- as you remember, we allowed Mr. Zigic to file, actually after the time that's specified in the Rules, his defence of alibi, but it says: "In which case the notification shall specify the place or places at which the accused claims to have been present at the time of the alleged crime and the names and addresses of witnesses and any other evidence upon which the accused intends to rely to establish the alibi." What would your explanation be of why this evidence wasn't put into that notification?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall try to give you a direct answer. To begin with, we received these documents at the time when the Prosecutor disclosed documents to us. Secondly, the witness today mentioned the beginning of July, and he claimed that he knew that at that time, Zigic was in detention. Therefore, we're trying to use the original document which was given us by the penitentiary at Banja Luka. We are merely trying to adduce the original document and are seeking its admission as the original document regarding that period of time. So we are not speaking about the alibi, but a fact that was indicated here, that was mentioned here by one of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But now I am asking you, Mr. Deretic. You, therefore, do not trust the witness. You need a document because, you see, we do have Rule 67. It is quite true. And at the end of it, and what you are trying to tell us, well formally, this is not the Defence of alibi but basically that is what it is, because that is what this document says. So the question is: Does it not -- are you not quite happy with the testimony of the witness? Is it that you need something to corroborate it further?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It suffices for Mr. Zigic's Defence, but I do not see why the testimony cannot be corroborated by an original document. That is the only reason why we are insisting on this, and it is up to the Chamber to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Deretic. You have to see whether it is possible or not in the light of our rules. So look at the Rule 67 and then perhaps it will be better. We shall not take the decision today, at least as speaking in my own name, I do not know what the opinion of my colleagues are there, but I am not in a position to decide upon it now. I need to think about it. Be that as it may, I should like to hear the arguments of both parties. You already told us what is your position. The Prosecutor, Ms. Somers, has already told us what she bases her objection on so we should like to know whether there is something else that you have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only, Mr. President, that my learned friend mentioned those periods of time only a fortnight ago and said that it was during those timeframes that certain incidents happened, and in relation to a written statement by the alleged camp commander, Mr. Sikirica. Because had it not been mentioned before, we would not be insisting on it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Could I clarify one thing with Ms. Somers. Since the rule that I just read talks about notification of place or places of which the accused claims to be present at the time of the alleged crime, refresh my recollection, are there crimes alleged in the indictment against Mr. Zigic that take place between July 1st and 9th apart from his being generally in the -- are there crimes that are alleged to take place in that time period?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I don't think there are specific. I think the general allegation as between such and such a date and such and such, but the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if -- just to let the Chamber know, if I have a chance to review very carefully the provision of the indictment, I will so inform the Chamber. I'm sorry I haven't memorised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Neither have I.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I believe we shall give it a thought and try to decide it tomorrow. As you understand, it is a matter which, if I may say so, which is not really something that arises every day and it is therefore something that warrants more consideration. So tomorrow -- we shall adjourn for the day and tomorrow we shall continue. But madam registrar, shall we be working in this courtroom or in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will be back in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, you have heard it. 9.20 Courtroom III.
